title: Atomic Energy Commission grant to Intelectron
place_text: Intelectron, Hell's Kitchen, New York City

tellings.quote: He gets a a grant for $300,000, which at the time would have been like at least a million dollars or more um from the Atomic Energy Commission,

plain: A researcher named Greg Malatzi, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a small company called Intelectron, based in the Hell's Kitchen neighbourhood of New York City in the early 1960s. He says it got a $300,000 grant, worth a million dollars or more today, from the Atomic Energy Commission, the US government agency that ran nuclear research at the time. He draws on the writer Annie Jacobsen and on the grant documents, and the point of the story is that, if true, the government took the company's unusual work seriously.
